name: Metformin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Metformin is cleared by the kidneys, and the risk of lactic acidosis rises as kidney function falls. The US label contraindicates it below an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 and advises against starting it at eGFR 30 to 45; guidelines cap the dose at 1,000 mg/day if it is continued at eGFR 30 to 44.

bands.recommendation: Usual dosing. Assess kidney function before starting and periodically (label).

eGFR 45–59: usual dose; consider dose reduction if at high risk of lactic acidosis. eGFR 30–44: label advises not to start; if continuing, reduce to a maximum of 1,000 mg/day (KDIGO 2022; ADA-KDIGO 2022). Recheck eGFR every 3 to 6 months.
Contraindicated (label). Stop if eGFR falls below 30.

crrt.text: Not appropriate; contraindicated in severe kidney impairment (label).

dialyzable: Yes: dialyzable with clearance up to 170 mL/min under good hemodynamic conditions; hemodialysis may help remove drug in suspected overdose (label).
monitoring: eGFR before starting and at least periodically; more often in older adults. Stop before or at the time of iodinated contrast in at-risk patients per label. Hold temporarily during acute illness with dehydration, sepsis, hypoxia or acute heart failure, during procedures with restricted food or fluid intake, and for acute kidney injury; restart when eating and kidney function is stable (label 5.1).

pediatric.approved_ages: Immediate-release: type 2 diabetes, 10 years and older (label). Extended-release (Glumetza): not established in pediatric patients.
pediatric.usual_dose: Immediate-release: 500 mg twice daily with meals; increase by 500 mg weekly (label).
pediatric.max_dose: 2,000 mg/day in two divided doses (immediate-release, label).

renal.recommendation: Immediate-release, 10 years and older: start 500 mg twice daily (label).
As for adults: eGFR 45–59 usual dose with monitoring; eGFR 30–44 do not start, and if continuing use a maximum of 1,000 mg/day (KDIGO 2022; ADA-KDIGO 2022).
renal.short: <45: do not start; cap if continuing

renal.recommendation: Contraindicated (label contraindication at eGFR <30 applies to all patients).

pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)

adult: Label chosen by the fetcher is GLUMETZA (extended-release, NDA021748). Most PH products are immediate-release; renal wording is class-wide in US labels but confirm against an IR label (Glucophage) once fetched.

KDIGO 2024 has metformin dosing practice points by eGFR (dose reduction in lower bands) that go beyond the label; not used here because the full text could not be verified in this session. Reviewer to decide whether to add them.
pediatric: The GLUMETZA label says pediatric use is not established. Immediate-release metformin labels have a pediatric type 2 diabetes indication; the IR label was not available to verify the age and dose, so none is stated. Re-draft pediatric block from the IR label.
